transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-10-28 15:00 PDT | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Alex Moore, Priya Shah (Redwood)  Jordan Lee, Maya Patel, Ravi Singh (Sunrise)

[00:00] Alex Moore: hey everybody, thanks for taking the time today, um this is Alex from Redwood, i'll give a quick overview, priya will jump into the console demo  sorry, uh, the rate limits and org keys walkthrough.
[00:08] Jordan Lee: yeah thanks, we appreciate it. we want to see how you do multi-tenant rate limiting and how we can enforce quotas per customer org.
[00:12] Priya Shah: great, i'll share my screen  um, if anyone can't see, say something. (screen share noise)
[00:22] Speaker 4: we can see it.
[00:25] Priya Shah: awesome. so first high-level: Redwood supports org-level keys and project keys, which you can use to separate tenants. we map usage and rate limits at the org or project scope, and you can attach policies  quota windows, burst capacity, and per-route overrides.
[00:42] Maya Patel: quick question  do you mean per-route like per-api-route, or per-model? we have different SLAs for embeddings vs. chat.
[00:48] Priya Shah: good call  yeah both. you can set quotas by route (example: /v1/chat vs /v1/embed) and by model or model family. for higher throughput models we usually recommend different limits and batching configs.
[01:02] Ravi Singh: how's enforcement implemented? is it a token bucket at the edge, or is it centralized in your control plane? we're worried about spoofing keys and edge bypass.
[01:12] Alex Moore: so enforcement is primarily at the runtime gateway  requests carry the org/project key, we check quotas in the routing path, there's an in-memory token bucket for low-latency checks and a backing store for long-term quotas. in the private/dedicated option you can run the enforcement in your VPC.
[01:28] Jordan Lee: and if a tenant spikes, can they burst above their quota temporarily?
[01:33] Priya Shah: yes, we support configurable burst policies  you can set a burst allowance that's consumed first, and you can also configure throttling behavior: hard deny, 429 with retry-after, or fallback to a smaller model.
[01:45] Speaker 5: fallback to smaller model sounds useful. how deterministic is that?
[01:49] Priya Shah: it's policy-driven. you can say if org X exceeds 80% of quota, route the request to a quantized model variant, or degrade to cached responses.
[01:59] Maya Patel: caching  do you do prefix or KV cache? what's shared?
[02:04] Priya Shah: we do prefix/K-V cache per project, and you can enable shared caches in a dedicated pool if you want cross-tenant dedupe. (small cough) apologies  sometimes our transcription says K V cache or K-V cash.
[02:18] Jordan Lee: haha yeah we noticed earlier docs had some typos.
[02:21] Alex Moore: totally. quick demo  console: this is the org's page, you create an org, then projects under it, each project gets API keys. you can assign role-based access (owner, admin, developer) and attach rate-limit profiles.
[02:36] [02:36] Priya Shah: clicking into the rate-limit profile  you can set qps, burst size, monthly token quota, per-route overrides, and enforcement action. here's an example profile for a 'standard' tenant: 50 qps, burst 200, monthly tokens 10M.
[02:52] Maya Patel: is monthly tokens tied to billing?
[02:55] Alex Moore: yes, billing ties to usage units; quotas can be a hard stop or soft alert before billing kicks in. we can also create alerts to notify when a tenant hits 75%, 90%.
[03:08] Ravi Singh: audit logs  do you log per-request metadata and key usage? retention windows?
[03:13] Priya Shah: yes, audit trails record request id, org, project, route, model, latency, and decision (allowed/denied/fallback). retention configurable; enterprise customers can push logs to their cloud storage or SIEM.
[03:25] Jordan Lee: do you have built-in SSO and RBAC for the console?
[03:28] Alex Moore: yes, SSO with SAML/OIDC, SCIM provisioning, and fine-grained RBAC. we also support API-only roles for service accounts.
[03:36] Speaker 4: sounds good. switching gears  how do org/project keys work with ingestion of PHI? we have strict requirements.
[03:43] Ravi Singh: right  we need KMS-managed keys and customers must control key rotation.
[03:47] Priya Shah: for Private/Dedicated deployments we integrate with your KMS/HSM; for hosted we offer customer-managed keys (bring your own key) for encryption at rest and audit for key access. note: on hosted we can also offer tenant-specific encryption if required.
[04:00] Jordan Lee: okay  timeline question: we want to pilot in prod-ish traffic for 3 tenants and then expand. can you support a pilot on hosted and migrate to dedicated with same keys?
[04:10] Alex Moore: yes, that's the typical flow. keys and policies can be exported and mapped in Dedicated. migration path is supported; we do a compatibility check and a cutover plan.
[04:18] Maya Patel: how are quotas looked up  is it eventual consistent? we're trying to avoid a scenario where two concurrent requests exceed quota because of race conditions.
[04:26] Priya Shah: good point  the in-memory token bucket has linearizable checks at runtime, we also have a short-consistency window between nodes; for hard limits we have global counters in the backing store. for strict enforcement we recommend dedicated capacity so counters are local and reduce cross-region latencies.
[04:40] Speaker 5: any rate limits at account-level versus org-level? like aggregate across projects?
[04:44] Priya Shah: yes you can set both org-level and project-level limits; project-level is evaluated first, then org-level as a global guard. you can also set route-level overrides.
[04:55] [05:00] Alex Moore: demo time  i'll show an example rule: create a rate-limit policy, set qps, burst, monthly units, set enforcement action to fallback to 'quantized-gpt-mini' model. now let's simulate with our traffic replay tool.
[05:12] [05:12] (tool noise)
[05:18] Priya Shah: the replay shows tenant A hitting bursts, token bucket consumed, then we hit fallback policy at 95% of quota and route to the smaller model. see the trace? latency spikes down for fallback.
[05:29] Jordan Lee: that helps. can we make the fallback return a cached summary instead of a model call?
[05:33] Priya Shah: yep  you can configure a cache-first policy which will check for cached responses before routing to a model. good for deterministic prompts and prompts where freshness isn't critical.
[05:42] Ravi Singh: for compliance we need to see how you redact logs  can you mask PII in traces?
[05:48] Priya Shah: we support redaction rules and hashing; logs for hosted by default redact content, and private customers can apply custom redaction, or route raw logs into their own storage behind KMS.
[05:59] Speaker 4: what's the behavior for sudden spikes  do you queue requests or return throttled errors?
[06:03] Alex Moore: configurable. options: immediate 429, queue up to x ms with backpressure, or degrade to lower-cost model. we recommend short queues plus graceful fallback to avoid cascading delays.
[06:14] Maya Patel: pricing impact  do rate limits affect billing granularity? like if a request is transformed to a smaller model via fallback, is billing based on the served model?
[06:23] Alex Moore: billed on the final model that executed; if we return a cached response there's no model cost. we'll include sample billing scenarios in the pricing sheet.
[06:31] [06:40] Priya Shah: quick aside  there are also org-level reserve tokens you can allocate for bursts, like a prepaid buffer, which is useful for tenants with spikey usage.
[06:49] Jordan Lee: can you show how to attach a rate-limit profile to a project via API?
[06:53] Priya Shah: sure  here's an API curl sample (transcribed): curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/orgs/ORG_ID/projects/PROJ_ID/ratelimits -H "Authorization: Bearer ORG_KEY" -d '{"qps":50,"burst":200,"monthly_tokens":10000000,"enforcement":"fallback"}' (note: transcription may mangle JSON quotes)
[07:13] Speaker 5: haha yeah we saw some quote escaping in the doc.
[07:18] Priya Shah: sorry about the transcript, but the API is straightforward. keys are long-lived or short-lived; you can create time-limited project keys for clients.
[07:27] Jordan Lee: that helps us reduce key blast-radius. what's your recommended pattern for multi-tenant clients? one org with multiple projects per tenant or one org per tenant?
[07:35] Alex Moore: typically one org per customer tenant and projects for environments (dev/stage/prod) or product lines. but if you need strict isolation for billing and quotas, you can also map differently. it's flexible.
[07:47] Ravi Singh: security again  are keys rotated automatically? is there a KMS integration for key generation?
[07:52] Priya Shah: we support automatic rotation and can integrate with your KMS for key material. on dedicated/private, keys never leave your cloud.
[07:59] [08:00] Alex Moore: time for a short Q&A, want to surface any blockers?
[08:04] Maya Patel: just one: we want to programmatically adjust quotas during promotional periods. can that be automated?
[08:10] Priya Shah: yes, quotas are exposed via API and can be updated; we also support scheduled rules and ramp policies.
[08:16] Jordan Lee: how do you handle cross-tenant payments and invoicing? need to pass usage back to our billing system per tenant.
[08:22] Alex Moore: we can export per-tenant usage CSVs or push to your billing endpoint; enterprise add-on includes per-tenant billing integration.
[08:31] Ravi Singh: what's the SLA for enforcement and audit logs?
[08:35] Priya Shah: standard SLA for hosted includes 99.9% uptime and log availability; dedicated SLA can be negotiated. logs can be replicated to your storage for compliance retention guarantees.
[08:46] [08:50] Speaker 4: okay let's talk about the PoC  scope would be 3 tenants, test their traffic patterns, validate fallback and billing metrics. estimated 2-3 weeks to stand up?
[08:59] Alex Moore: yep  Priya will prepare a PoC config. low friction: we can spin up a trial org, generate org/project keys for your tenants, and run replay against staged traffic.
[09:09] Priya Shah: i'll also share our replay tool and a test harness. we can simulate spikes and demonstrate quota enforcement.
[09:16] Jordan Lee: for the pilot we need to validate that we can migrate to dedicated without major code changes. is that a big lift?
[09:22] Alex Moore: migration is mostly configuration  same API surface. we'll validate compatibility during the PoC and provide a migration plan.
[09:29] Maya Patel: any limitations around per-route limits with streaming responses? we use streaming for chat.
[09:34] Priya Shah: streaming is supported; rate limiting counts tokens emitted and requests. there's special handling for in-flight streams to avoid partial-charges and to ensure graceful cancellation. slight differences in enforcement model but supported.
[09:47] Speaker 5: transcription note: sometimes model names were misheard  e.g., "Redwood Dedicate" in transcript should read Redwood Dedicated.
[09:53] Alex Moore: noted. small demo wrap-up  i'll send the one-pager and pricing examples, Priya will send config and scripts.
[09:59] [10:00] Priya Shah: closing with a quick security mention: our security page has SOC2, ISO references; we'll attach the security pack.
[10:06] Ravi Singh: please include details on KMS, HSM support and log retention.
[10:10] Alex Moore: will do. last question from Jordan?
[10:14] Jordan Lee: nothing else, thanks  plan to review docs and pick tenant list.
[10:17] Alex Moore: perfect. recap: one-pager + pricing, PoC config, trial account setup, security follow-up. thanks everyone.
[10:24] (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: speaker labels occasionally generic (Speaker 4/5), small mis-transcriptions (K-V cache, Redwood Dedicate). Periodic timestamps roughly every 30-90s to reflect Fireflies pattern.
